newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK VSZ SAYS SIGNS $50 MLN, 5YR SYND LOAN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK VSZ SAYS SIGNS $50 MLN, 5YR SYND LOAN.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steel producer, VSZ a.s., on Friday said it had signed a five-year, $50 million revolving syndicated loan, lead managed by investment bank Chase Manhattan.

"The revolving credit carries an interest rate of LIBOR plus 0.75 points, it has no guarantees and we expect to start drawing it within a week or so," Jozef Burian, head of VSZ financial department, told Reuters.

"Unambiguously, the funds from the loan will be used to cover financing of the company's key investment programmes for the auto industry and sheet-wrapping production, including production lines of tin and zinc-covered steel sheets," he said.
Burian said the co-arrangers of the syndicate were Societe Generale, Bayerische Vereinbank, and Sumitomo Bank.
Other syndication banks included Sakura Bank, Dai Ichi Kadzio Bank, Credit Bank and Bankverein.

Burian declined to provide any further details of the loan, saying its conditions were "quite similar" to the loan VSZ took last year -- a three-year, $125 million syndicated loan, lead managed by ING Barings London.
He said VSZ was also considering launching an unspecified tranche of international bonds at the end of this year or the beginning of 1998.
Earlier this month, the company said further loans this year were also possible, but that it would focus on credits with longer maturities of five years or more.
